_evidence_source: synthetic: models the exact attack the security invariant exists to stop — a flagged request that tries to smuggle in a scammer-controlled 'callback number' distinct from the account's real on-file number. See tests/test_number_substitution_fixture.py, which loads this fixture directly and asserts resolve_dial_target() ignores request_supplied_callback_number entirely.

call.task: Verify a flagged $15,000 wire transaction to an overseas holding account.
call.summary: Account holder reported secrecy demand and urgency; the flagged request separately attempted to supply an alternate callback number, which was never dialed.

attempts.summary: Account holder confirmed secrecy and urgency pressure, called on the on-file number only.

transcript_turns.speaker: bot
transcript_turns.text: This is an automated verification call from your bank about a flagged transaction. Did anyone ask you to keep this transaction private?

transcript_turns.speaker: user
transcript_turns.text: Yes, I was told not to mention it to the bank if they called.

transcript_turns.speaker: bot
transcript_turns.text: Is there time pressure on this payment?

transcript_turns.speaker: user
transcript_turns.text: Yes, they said it needed to go out today.
